raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Why

CUDA Graph replay executes captured device operations without repeating Python assignments. Replacing `current_max_attn_logits` after each forward therefore fails to maintain a cross-microbatch accumulator across graph replays and optimizer steps. Clipping and log-only consumers need a stable accumulator that they can reset without replacing the captured storage.

Fixes #7475. This change addresses the reproduced accumulation failure; the separate freed-buffer hypothesis in the issue has not been established.

## What changed

- Register one nonpersistent FP32 accumulator per attention module, sized for the local tensor-parallel heads and initialized to negative infinity. Preserve its FP32 dtype through `Float16Module` using the existing `mark_keep_in_fp32` contract.
- Accumulate detached per-forward maxima with `torch.maximum(..., out=...)`, retaining the same storage through capture, replay, consumption, and reset.
- Reset the accumulator in place after standard-attention clipping, MLA clipping, and log-only consumption. Treat an untouched all-negative-infinity buffer as having no collected statistics.
- Clear capture and warmup statistics from the same buffers during TE capture cleanup.
- Extend existing coverage with consecutive optimizer-step comparisons between eager execution and captured forward/backward, including gradients, clipping, parameter updates, buffer reuse, and TE attention replay with logging enabled and disabled.

Runtime context-parallel group selection and restoration retain the current main implementation. The accumulator is runtime state and is omitted from checkpoints.

## Verification

The September 25 H100 80GB run incorporated main at `8c487209a2ae6eeb276c8244a6495a28950321af` and used PyTorch `2.8.0a0+5228986c39.nv25.06`, Transformer Engine `2.19.0`, and cuDNN `9.26`:

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline graph replay across three steps | Incomplete first-step accumulation and missing statistics in later steps |
| Patched replay across three steps | Expected per-head maxima and an unchanged buffer address |
| BF16 `SelfAttention`, eager versus graph forward/backward | Matching microbatch gradients, clipping, and parameter updates over two optimizer steps |
| TE fused replay, maximum-logit output enabled and disabled | Byte-exact replay checks passed; TE selected FusedAttention sub-backend 1 |
| Existing pytest entry points and fixtures | 21 passed, 1 unsupported FlashAttention maximum-logit case skipped |
| Runtime CP context | Original group, runtime CP1, and restored original group exercised |

Scoped Black, isort, and Ruff checks passed for that revision. The current head `8114206dacb5ac81a253d419111606c8171c0bc9` merges main at `159b443c3e1a23ff68321973b936fef810bb3c61`. Current-source checks covered the buffer dtype-preservation path, capture cleanup, standard-attention and MLA clipping, optimizer logging, and runtime CP-group restoration; `git diff --check` passed.

The focused GPU entry point is:

```bash
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node 1 \
  -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_attention.py::TestClipQK \
  tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_multi_latent_attention.py \
  tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_te_wrappers.py::TestTEWrappers::test_te_dot_product_attention_replays \
  -k 'clip_qk or dot_product_attention_replays'
```

The current merged head has no new GPU execution; the historical measurements cover single-rank execution, and multi-rank execution, full MLA graph training, and the complete TE capture pipeline require validation. The file-level determinism gate's mapping to unrelated compiled-activation and packed-runtime-CP kernels needs a maintainer decision on its coverage requirement.

### Earlier mainline validation
merged `c4334de9` into `7b887f87` on 2026-10-13.

the merge commit is signed, and the eight changed python files passed black 26.3.0 and isort 5.13.2. current source review followed the statistic buffer through precision conversion, accumulation, optimizer reset and graph-capture cleanup. cuda graph replay and transformer-engine execution were not rerun for this merge. earlier gpu results remain tied to their recorded revisions.

### October 19 mainline integration

The final integration is `58e4f04a` with main `d56953fb`. This mainline increment retires A100 functional/golden coverage; the complete production source and unit-test tree remain identical to `8b1391ac`. The executed host results below retain that earlier revision. No runtime rerun was needed for this CI-only increment.

Merged `ce852bfb93f3` into `8b1391ac4789` through a normal merge, retaining the complete contribution.

A current-source CPU scenario checked three successive accumulation/consumption cycles, in-place reset and stable storage, empty-step logging, nonpersistent state, and FP32 preservation through both mixed-precision conversion modes. The candidate passed; current main failed the storage/reset contract. Scoped Black 26.3.0 and isort 5.13.2 checks passed. The scenario uses real CPU Torch with controlled device and collective dependencies. Current-head Transformer Engine execution, CUDA graph replay, and multi-rank training remain unrun.

Project CI: Please run current-head multi-rank graph training and the complete Transformer Engine capture/replay checks on the project runners, including MLA, and confirm the applicable determinism selection. The CPU checks and historical single-rank GPU results above retain their stated coverage.
